summary: Feed s155_double to IDS is degraded: 29.1% of frames truncated to ~192 bytes (IDS needs full payload) and 80.2% of bytes encrypted (exceeds 60% IDS tolerance), both severely limiting detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is slicing / snap-length truncating frames to ~192 bytes (795 of 2729 frames, 29.1% > 5% threshold), likely a broker slicing policy to save bandwidth.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature and anomaly detection; truncated payloads prevent payload inspection, reassembly and file extraction, causing missed detections.

recommended_fix.why: IDS requires full payload per tool profile; disable slicing / set snaplen to 1518+ to forward complete frames to IDS.

findings.root_cause: 80.2% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/QUIC), well above the 60% this IDS can tolerate without decryption; traffic is forwarded encrypted with no broker-side decryption.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS is blind to payload inside encryption; cannot apply signatures or detect exploits/malware in encrypted streams, reducing effective coverage to metadata only.

recommended_fix.why: IDS cannot inspect encrypted payload; decrypt relevant TLS centrally (with proper keys/policy) and feed cleartext to IDS, or supplement with decrypted feed / NDR with JA3/JA4 and metadata analytics.
